description: Second-order linear homogeneous ODE with constant coefficients: ay'' + by' + cy = 0. Covers the superposition principle (and its proof), forming the characteristic equation via the y = e^(lambda x) ansatz, the three discriminant cases (Delta > 0, = 0, < 0) and their general-solution forms, and fully-worked examples for each case.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 differential-equations lesson chapter (PHANKIMSIE booklet) — lesson definitions, theorems, and fully worked examples, photographed pages
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from photographed textbook pages (Claude Code), 2026-08-27

lessons.title: Superposition principle for ay'' + by' + cy = 0
lessons.statement_latex: \text{If } f_1, f_2 \text{ are solutions of } ay''+by'+cy=0, \text{ then } y = c_1f_1 + c_2f_2 \text{ is also a solution, for any } c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.
solution_steps: \text{Since } f_1, f_2 \text{ solve the homogeneous equation: } af_1''+bf_1'+cf_1 = 0 \text{ and } af_2''+bf_2'+cf_2 = 0
lessons.answer_latex: \text{So } y = c_1f_1 + c_2f_2 \text{ is the general solution of } ay''+by'+cy=0.

lessons.title: Forming the characteristic equation
solution_steps: \text{Ansatz: } y = e^{\lambda x} \implies y' = \lambda e^{\lambda x},\ y'' = \lambda^2 e^{\lambda x}
a\lambda^2 e^{\lambda x} + b\lambda e^{\lambda x} + ce^{\lambda x} = 0
lessons.answer_latex: a\lambda^2 + b\lambda + c = 0 \quad \text{(the characteristic equation)},\quad \Delta = b^2-4ac,\quad \lambda = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}

lessons.title: General solution of ay'' + by' + cy = 0 by discriminant sign
lessons.statement_latex: (E):\ ay''+by'+cy=0,\quad a\neq 0,\ a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}. \text{ Characteristic equation } a\lambda^2+b\lambda+c=0 \text{ has roots } \lambda_1, \lambda_2.
solution_steps: \text{If } \Delta > 0\text{: two distinct real roots } \lambda_1=\alpha,\ \lambda_2=\beta \implies y = Ae^{\alpha x} + Be^{\beta x},\ A,B\in\mathbb{R}
\text{If } \Delta = 0\text{: a repeated real root } \lambda_1=\lambda_2=\alpha \implies y = (Ax+B)e^{\alpha x},\ A,B\in\mathbb{R}
\text{If } \Delta < 0\text{: complex conjugate roots } \lambda = \alpha \pm i\beta \implies y = e^{\alpha x}(A\cos\beta x + B\sin\beta x),\ A,B\in\mathbb{R}

lessons.title: Three-part drill: one example per discriminant case
lessons.answer_latex: \text{ក. } y = Ae^{\frac{2}{3}x}+Be^{-2x} \qquad \text{ខ. } y = e^{\frac{3}{2}x}\left(A\cos\tfrac{1}{2}x+B\sin\tfrac{1}{2}x\right) \qquad \text{គ. } y = (Ax+B)e^{2x},\quad A,B\in\mathbb{R}
